title: Lesson 24: Performance: Query Optimization, Selective SOQL, Indexes, and Caching
description: How a query becomes fast: the selectivity thresholds the optimizer uses to decide whether an index is worth it, how to write SOQL that the optimizer will actually treat well, how to measure and index, and Platform Cache as the lever that skips the query entirely.

questions.question: Why can a query on an indexed field still run as a full scan?
options: Indexed fields stop being used once a table grows past a million rows
The optimizer picks between an index and a scan at random
Only queries that sort on the indexed field can use that index
A negative operator or broad filter makes the query non-selective
questions.explanation: The optimizer weighs the filter's selectivity, so an indexed field filtered with a negative or broad condition is treated as non-selective and scanned.

questions.question: Before investing in a custom index, what should the architect do?
options: Index every field that the slow query happens to filter on
Move the whole query into a scheduled batch job
Measure the field's selectivity before adding an index
Add a second filter on the same field to narrow it
questions.explanation: Indexing pays off only when the filter is selective against the threshold; indexing a low-selectivity field is wasted because the optimizer ignores it.

questions.question: When is Platform Cache the right lever?
options: For large result sets that must always stay fully up to date
For small stable values read far more often than they change
For per-user values that change on every request
For values that the application code itself mutates on every transaction
questions.explanation: Caching removes the need to run the query at all, so it fits values that are stable and hot rather than large or rapidly changing ones.
